drivingQuestion: Why is a consecrated purchased field redeemed at its market value rather than by the fifty-shekel-per-sowing-area formula stated for an ancestral field?
outcomeNote: The baraita settles the mishna's ruling: מכסת means the sum of the field's worth, so the fifty-shekel formula is confined to an ancestral field.

segments.he: שְׂדֵה מִקְנָה נוֹתֵן שׇׁוְויוֹ. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״בְּמִכְסַת״ — מַה בָּא לִלְמוֹד? לְפִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״זֶרַע חֹמֶר שְׂעוֹרִים בַּחֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כָּסֶף״, יָכוֹל אַף שְׂדֵה מִקְנָה כֵּן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״מִכְסַת״.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: And with regard to «a purchased field» that one consecrates, «he gives its value» as redemption, a sum that can be more or less than fifty silver shekels for an area required for the sowing of a kor of barley seed. «The Sages taught» in a baraita: The verse states: “Then the priest shall reckon for him the «worth» of your valuation until the Jubilee Year; and he shall give your valuation in that day, as a holy thing to the Lord” (Leviticus 27:23). «What does this» word “worth” «come to teach? Since it is stated» with regard to an ancestral field: “An area fit for the «sowing of a ḥomer of barley seed is redeemed for fifty silver shekels”» (Leviticus 27:16), one «might» have thought that «a purchased field is also» redeemed using «this» formula. Therefore, «the verse states “worth,”» which means the market value of the field.
